full_judgment: 28. It has been held in the case of Pathan vs Poonrulli. A 19701 57 that even in the absence of any move by the parties the Court can stio-nrotu make the correction. It is confined only to the kind of mistakes, errors, slips of omissions mentioned therein. Where the decree is not in conformity with the judgment the Court can order correction even when the decree has been executed and fully satisfied. It is held in the case of Kudu vs Bhim. A 1950 P 183 that Commissioners' mistake in totaling area embodied in decree may be corrected. Decision has been passed in the case of Narayan Das vs Bishnu. A 1963 that a decree can be corrected, even when it is executed. In the light of the decision passed in the case of Adinarayana vs Kothanda, A 1940, the High Court can interfere with in special circumstances in revision. It is held in the case of Chandra vs Sudhangshu A 1924 C 895.28 CWN 873 that it is the duty of the Court to amend the decree when it is brought to its notice that it does not agree with the judgment and the power was held to be discretionary.
